knowledge:
- key_parameters: memSubjects=A vector of length equal to the number of subjects, where 1 indicates case and 0 indicates control ;; transformFlag=Logical flag indicating whether to apply data transformation (e.g., Box-Cox) ;; transformMethod=Character string specifying the transformation method, typically 'boxcox' ;; scaleFlag=Logical flag indicating whether to scale the gene expression levels ;; quiet=Logical flag to suppress progress messages during EM optimization ;; iniGeneMethod=Method to initialize gene clustering ('Ttest' or 'Wilcox') in gsMMD/gsMMD.default ;; memIni=A vector of initial gene cluster memberships (1=over-expressed, 2=non-differentially expressed, 3=under-expressed) for gsMMD2/gsMMD2.default
- alternatives: eLNN and eGG (Lo and Gottardo, 2007)=Empirical Bayes models for differential gene expression ;; standard two-sample t-test or Wilcoxon rank-sum test=Simple non-model-based alternatives, though they do not directly estimate FDR, FNDR, FPR, and FNR for the specific dataset
- when_to_use: Use when analyzing transcriptomics/microarray data with exactly two tissue types (case vs. control) and where tissue samples within a tissue type are conditionally independent given the gene (marginal correlations are close to zero). It is especially useful when you need direct estimates of dataset-specific error rates (FDR, FNDR, FPR, FNR).
- pitfalls: The EM optimization can be computationally slow for very large datasets, though v2.0.7+ utilizes Fortran code to improve speed ;; Visualizing goodness of fit via plotHistDensity assumes that marginal correlations among tissue samples are ignorable/close to zero ;; memSubjects must be strictly coded as 0 (control) and 1 (case)

workflows.name: expression_set_workflow
workflows.intent: Select differentially expressed genes, estimate error rates, and plot model fit from an ExpressionSet object.
input: eSet1 (ExpressionSet object containing gene expression data and phenotypic metadata)
workflows.stages: 1. Prepare sample membership vector ;; 2. Run gene selection using gsMMD ;; 3. Estimate error rates using errRates ;; 4. Plot density fit using plotHistDensity
workflows.code:
library(GeneSelectMMD)
  library(ALL)
  data(ALL)
  eSet1 <- ALL[1:100, ALL$BT == "B3" | ALL$BT == "T2"]
  
  mem.str <- as.character(eSet1$BT)
  nSubjects <- length(mem.str)
  memSubjects <- rep(0,nSubjects)
  # B3 coded as 0, T2 coded as 1
  memSubjects[mem.str == "T2"] <- 1
  
  obj.gsMMD <- gsMMD(eSet1, memSubjects, transformFlag = TRUE, 
    transformMethod = "boxcox", scaleFlag = TRUE, quiet = TRUE)
  para <- obj.gsMMD$para
  print(round(para, 3))
  print(round(errRates(obj.gsMMD), 3))
  plotHistDensity(obj.gsMMD, plotFlag = "case", 
      mytitle = "Histogram of gene expression levels for T2\nimposed with estimated density (case)", 
      plotComponent = TRUE, 
      x.legend = c(0.8, 3), 
      y.legend = c(0.3, 0.4), 
      numPoints = 500,
      cex.main = 1,
      cex = 1)

workflows.name: data_matrix_workflow
workflows.intent: Select differentially expressed genes and estimate error rates from a raw expression matrix.
input: mat (matrix of gene expression values where rows are genes and columns are samples)
workflows.stages: 1. Prepare sample membership vector ;; 2. Run gene selection using gsMMD.default ;; 3. Estimate error rates using errRates
workflows.code:
library(GeneSelectMMD)
  library(ALL)
  data(ALL)
  eSet1 <- ALL[1:100, ALL$BT == "B3" | ALL$BT == "T2"]
  mat <- exprs(eSet1)
  
  mem.str <- as.character(eSet1$BT)
  nSubjects <- length(mem.str)
  memSubjects <- rep(0,nSubjects)
  # B3 coded as 0, T2 coded as 1
  memSubjects[mem.str == "T2"] <- 1
 
  obj.gsMMD <- gsMMD.default(mat, memSubjects, iniGeneMethod = "Ttest",
          transformFlag = TRUE, transformMethod = "boxcox", scaleFlag = TRUE,
          quiet=TRUE)
  para <- obj.gsMMD$para
  print(round(para, 3))
  print(round(errRates(obj.gsMMD), 3))
